# Shehbaz Sharif, Pakistan, 2024: 1B.7 evidence note

Overall read: **mildly favorable, low-to-moderate confidence**. I found 2024 evidence that Pakistan under Sharif continued to emphasize formal nuclear-safety, arms-control, and disarmament institutions. I did **not** find reliable 2024 evidence that Sharif surrounded nuclear/security decisions with ideological loyalists or deliberately downgraded expert institutions.

| Polarity | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable page URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Favorable | Pakistan’s nuclear-security regime page | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | Updated in May 2024; standing page | https://mofa.gov.pk/vienna-pakistans-nuclear-safety-seccurity-regime | The official page says the NCA is chaired by the prime minister, the SPD serves as secretariat, and Pakistan updated its nuclear-security regime booklet in May 2024 and renewed practical arrangements with the IAEA. This supports an institutional, expert-run command-and-control structure rather than a personality-driven one. | 1B.7; also 1B.3, 1B.4 |
| Favorable | 6th Round of Pakistan-UK Dialogue on Arms Control and Non-Proliferation | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | 2024-05-16 | https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/6th-round-of-pakistan-uk-dialogue-on-arms-control-non-proliferation | Pakistan held a formal bilateral dialogue on arms control and nonproliferation and discussed UN, CD, IAEA, and OPCW issues. That is evidence of reliance on diplomatic and technical institutions for nuclear-security policy. | 1B.7; also 1B.4 |
| Favorable | Pakistan-China Bilateral Consultations on Arms Control and Nonproliferation | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | 2024-09-14 | https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/pakistan-china-bilateral-consultations-on-arms-control-and-nonproliferation | The government sustained structured consultations covering global/regional security, cyber, AI, outer space, peaceful nuclear technology, and multilateral treaty forums. This points to expert-led institutional engagement rather than ideologue-led decision making. | 1B.7; also 1B.4 |
| Favorable | The visit of UN Disarmament Fellows to Pakistan | Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan | 2024-10-21 | https://mofa.gov.pk/press-releases/the-visit-of-un-disarmament-fellows-to-pakistan | Pakistan briefed UN disarmament fellows on arms control, disarmament, nonproliferation, and its nuclear safety/security architecture. That is direct evidence of investment in technical knowledge and verification-oriented institutions. | 1B.7; also 1B.4, 1B.3 |
| Favorable | Message on the Occasion of Youm-e-Takbeer on 28th May 2024 | Press Information Department, Pakistan | 2024-05-27 | https://pid.gov.pk/site/press_detail/25454 | The government described Pakistan as a responsible nuclear state committed to stringent controls, comprehensive safety measures, and Credible Minimum Deterrence. This is institutional language, not cult-of-personality rhetoric, and it supports a risk-managed posture. | 1B.7; also 1B.3, 1B.5, 1B.6 |
| Favorable | PM voices satisfaction over Pakistan Army’s operational preparedness | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-05 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/05-09-2024/pm-expresses-satisfaction-over-pak-armys-operational-preparedness | Sharif praised preparedness and framed it as preserving the balance of power necessary for peace in nuclearized South Asia. This is not a staffing decision, but it is consistent with a professionalized deterrence mindset rather than ad hoc ideological control. | 1B.7; also 1B.5 |

## Search gap

- I did **not** find credible 2024 evidence that Sharif replaced expert nuclear/security institutions with loyalists or ideologues.
- I also did **not** find a 2024 instance where he personally elevated a single loyalist over technical authorities in a way that clearly affected nuclear/security governance.
- The evidence base is therefore mostly **institutional and indirect**: it supports a reading of continued reliance on expert bodies, but not a strong ruler-specific personnel reform story.
